name: Greek Lemon Chicken with Roasted Potatoes
summary: Marinate chicken in lemon, garlic, and oregano, then roast over potatoes until golden.
technique_notes: Marinate chicken in the lemon-oil-oregano blend ~2 hours. Spread potatoes in the dish, lay chicken skin-side up on top, and roast at 425°F for only 10 minutes, then drop to 375°F for 45-55 minutes to 185°F internal (425°F throughout is too hot for the long bake). Rest 10-15 minutes; broil briefly to crisp skin.

name: Sheet-Pan Salmon with Lemon and Asparagus
summary: Roast salmon and asparagus on one pan with olive oil, lemon, and herbs.
technique_notes: Roast skin-side down at 400°F, 10-15 min, pulling salmon at 120-130°F internal (instant-read) for medium-rare so it stays moist. Arrange asparagus around the perimeter, salmon in the center; match thin spears to the short cook time. Pat salmon dry and squeeze lemon on after roasting, not before.

name: Shakshuka (Eggs Poached in Spiced Tomato Sauce)
summary: Simmer peppers and tomatoes with cumin and paprika, poach eggs in the sauce, finish with feta.
technique_notes: Saute onions and peppers over high heat, mostly undisturbed (~6 min, then ~4 more), so they char and tenderize without turning sweet; add garlic, then bloom paprika and cumin 30 sec. Simmer sauce 10 min. Make wells, spoon sauce over the whites, cover on lowest heat 5-8 min until whites set, yolks runny.

name: Greek Salad with Chickpeas
summary: Toss cucumber, tomato, olives, and chickpeas with feta and a red-wine vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Rinse canned chickpeas to cut sodium. Use firm English or Persian cucumbers (thin-skinned, few seeds) so the salad holds up. Whisk the EVOO-lemon dressing in the bowl first, then toss everything to coat. Use fresh lemon over bottled for brighter flavor. Authentic Greek versions skip lettuce.

name: Mediterranean Lentil Soup
summary: Simmer green lentils with mirepoix, cumin, and tomato; stir in spinach and lemon at the end.
technique_notes: Hold the acid (lemon and most of the tomato) until the lentils are fully tender; acid added early keeps lentils hard. Soften the mirepoix first, and stir spinach in at the very end off the heat so it just wilts.

name: Mediterranean Quinoa Bowl with Feta and Cucumber
summary: Layer quinoa with chickpeas, chopped veg, feta, and a lemon-tahini drizzle.
technique_notes: Rinse quinoa well under cold water to wash off bitter saponins. Add the still-warm cooked quinoa to the lemon vinaigrette so it absorbs the dressing, then let it cool completely before stirring in the cold vegetables so they stay crisp. Top with feta last.

name: Baked Cod with Tomatoes, Olives, and Capers
summary: Bake cod in a puttanesca-style tomato, olive, and caper sauce.
technique_notes: Build the sauce on the stovetop first: saute onion (fennel) 7-9 min until soft, add garlic 1 min, then tomatoes and olives, simmering ~2 min to thicken. Pat cod dry and season, nestle it into the sauce spooning some over the top, then bake at 350°F just 6-8 min until it flakes. Go easy on salt.

name: Baked Falafel Bowls with Tahini
summary: Bake spiced chickpea falafel and serve over greens with cucumber, tomato, and tahini sauce.
technique_notes: Soak dried chickpeas (with a little baking soda) overnight, 18+ hrs, until one crushes easily; never use canned. Drain and pat very dry (excess moisture makes them gooey). Pulse coarse, not pureed, and chill 1+ hr so they hold shape without egg or flour. Oil the pan, brush tops, bake 350°F 8 min, flip, 7-12 min more.

name: Tuscan White Bean and Kale Stew
summary: Simmer white beans with kale, garlic, and tomato into a hearty rosemary-scented stew.
technique_notes: Soften onion, carrot, and celery ~8 min, then garlic 1 min. Simmer soaked beans 45-50 min until nearly tender before adding kale and tomatoes; kale needs another 30-45 min to soften. A Parmesan rind simmered in adds savory depth (freeze rinds up to 6 months). Stir in vinegar and salt only at the very end.

name: Chicken Souvlaki with Tzatziki
summary: Grill lemon-oregano chicken skewers; serve with cucumber-yogurt tzatziki and a chopped salad.
technique_notes: Marinate even chicken cubes in the lemon-vinegar-garlic-oregano dressing ~2 hrs, reserving some dressing (unmixed) for the salad. Salt the cucumber and drain ~30 min, then pat dry before mixing into Greek yogurt so the tzatziki stays thick. Don't crowd skewers; grill over medium-high to 155°F internal (~5 min), rest 3 min.

name: Turkey and Brown Rice Stuffed Bell Peppers
summary: Stuff peppers with spiced turkey, brown rice, and tomato; bake until tender.
technique_notes: Brown the turkey with onion and spices, simmer with tomato sauce and broth, then mix with fully cooked rice (not par-cooked). Halve raw peppers lengthwise, fill, set in the dish with broth poured in the bottom, cover tightly with foil, and bake at 400°F about 45 minutes until tender, then uncover to finish.

name: Whole Wheat Pasta with Cherry Tomatoes, White Beans, and Basil
summary: Burst cherry tomatoes in olive oil and garlic, toss with pasta, white beans, and basil.
technique_notes: Cook the cherry tomatoes in olive oil in a covered skillet over medium heat 6-12 minutes until most burst and the oil turns red; this becomes the light sauce. Stir in drained al dente whole wheat pasta off the heat, fold beans in gently, then rest ~20 minutes so the pasta absorbs the sauce. Add basil last.

name: Mujadara (Lentils and Rice with Crispy Onions)
summary: Cook lentils and rice with cumin; top with deeply caramelized onions and a yogurt dollop.
technique_notes: Par-boil lentils ~10-12 min until just tender, then drain. Caramelize the diced onions deeply for about 40 min until darker than normal caramelized (this gives the golden hue), reserve thin onion rings to fry separately in shimmering oil for the crisp garnish. Rinse and soak rice, add with lentils, simmer covered 15-20 min, then rest 10 min.

name: Grilled Mediterranean Chicken Salad
summary: Slice grilled chicken over greens with cucumber, tomato, olives, and a lemon vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Marinate chicken in a yogurt-lemon-garlic mix at least 30 minutes (overnight is better). Toss the greens, cucumber and feta with most of the dressing, reserving some. Sear chicken undisturbed ~5 minutes per side to 165°F, shaking off excess marinade first so it browns. Plate salad, top with sliced chicken, drizzle reserved dressing, serve at once.

name: Salmon Niçoise-Style Salad
summary: Compose seared salmon with blanched green beans, eggs, potatoes, and a dijon vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Blanch green beans just 1.5 minutes, then ice-bath. Boil potatoes until barely tender, then steam off-heat under a towel 15-20 minutes. Rather than searing, you can marinate salmon in lemon-mustard 15 minutes and roast at 500°F for 12-15 minutes, resting 15 minutes before flaking. Compose the platter, don't toss.

name: Tabbouleh with Grilled Chicken
summary: Toss a parsley-forward bulgur tabbouleh with lemon and olive oil; top with sliced grilled chicken.
technique_notes: It's parsley-forward with bulgur as an accent. Chop herbs by hand with a sharp knife — a food processor bruises them and turns the salad soggy. For fine bulgur, soak (don't boil) in cold water ~20 min until tender, then drain well. Flavor improves as it rests; keeps up to 3 days chilled.

name: Eggplant and Chickpea Tagine
summary: Stew eggplant and chickpeas with warm spices and a touch of dried fruit; serve over couscous or farro.
technique_notes: Brown the eggplant in batches until golden on all sides but not soft inside. Fry onion, ginger and spices until softened, then add tomatoes, stock, honey and the apricots; nestle the eggplant in and simmer covered ~30 minutes until tender. (Source adds apricots at the start, not partway through.)

name: Yogurt-Marinated Grilled Chicken with Farro
summary: Marinate chicken in spiced yogurt and grill; serve over farro with a herb salad.
technique_notes: Pound breasts to even thickness, then marinate in the yogurt-lemon-garlic mix at least 2 hours and up to 24. Let the chicken sit at room temperature ~20 minutes before cooking, then grill over high heat to 160-165°F, flipping once. Toast the farro before simmering for nuttier flavor.

name: Teriyaki Salmon Bowl with Brown Rice and Edamame
summary: Glaze salmon with a light teriyaki, serve over brown rice with edamame and cucumber.
technique_notes: Marinate salmon 30-60 minutes, then cook through (broil ~6 inches from heat 3-4 minutes, or air fry 400°F 5-7 minutes) until caramelized at the edges. Simmer the reserved marinade separately into a glaze and drizzle on at the end - this also cooks off any raw-fish bacteria - rather than brushing during a brief broil.

name: Thai-Inspired Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry
summary: Stir-fry chicken and crisp vegetables in a garlic-ginger-fish-sauce glaze; serve over brown rice.
technique_notes: Cook over the highest heat in batches so the chicken sears instead of steaming. Add vegetables by density (peppers before snap peas) and stir in the basil off the heat at the very end so it stays fragrant.

name: Korean-Style Beef Bowl (Bulgogi)
summary: Sear thin-sliced marinated beef; serve over brown rice with quick-pickled cucumber and greens.
technique_notes: Slice the beef very thin against the grain (freeze 20 min first; kitchen shears help) and use grated pear or onion to tenderize. Marinate 1 hour up to 1 day. Cook in batches over medium-high heat about 5 minutes, adding a little honey at the end to caramelize; sear hard without crowding.

name: Vietnamese Chicken Lettuce Wraps
summary: Saute ground chicken with ginger and lime; spoon into lettuce cups with shredded carrot and herbs.
technique_notes: Spread the ground chicken and brown undisturbed about 6 minutes, then break up and cook 6-8 more until browned. Stir in shallots/chilies 30 seconds, then pull off heat and fold in the lime-fish-sauce-sugar mix with herbs to keep it bright. Keep filling and herbs separate from the lettuce until eating.

name: Miso-Glazed Cod with Bok Choy
summary: Broil miso-glazed cod and serve with quick-seared bok choy and brown rice.
technique_notes: Marinate the cod in the miso 4-8 hours or overnight. Cook bok choy cut-side down in oil plus a splash of water until the water evaporates and it caramelizes, 6-7 min, then add garlic and vinegar 1-2 min. Broil cod about 8 min, rotating halfway; the miso sugars char fast, so watch closely.

name: Ginger Chicken with Soba Noodles
summary: Toss seared ginger chicken and vegetables with soba in a light soy-sesame sauce.
technique_notes: Cook soba just to al dente (~5 minutes), then drain and rinse well under cool water to wash off surface starch and stop the cooking, preventing gummy clumps. Add the snap peas to boiling water for only ~20 seconds so they stay crisp-tender before draining.

name: Sesame Tofu and Broccoli Stir-Fry
summary: Crisp tofu and stir-fry with broccoli in a garlic-sesame-soy sauce over brown rice.
technique_notes: Press the tofu at least 30 min, cut into 1-inch cubes, salt, then toss with cornstarch (about 2 Tbsp) for crispness. Heat the pan before adding oil so cubes don't stick, and fry golden on each side. The cornstarch sauce thickens fast, so add broccoli, then sauce, and fold the tofu back in off the heat.

name: Black Bean and Sweet Potato Tacos
summary: Roast cumin-spiced sweet potato, fold into tortillas with black beans, avocado, and lime slaw.
technique_notes: Cut sweet potato into 1/2-inch cubes, toss with oil/chili/cumin, and roast at 425°F in a single uncrowded layer; flip at 15 min and roast 15 more until edges crisp. Warm tortillas in a dry skillet, covered to stay soft. Dress the slaw with its acid only just before serving.

name: Chicken Fajita Bowls
summary: Sear fajita-spiced chicken and peppers; build bowls with brown rice, beans, and avocado.
technique_notes: Toss chicken and peppers in spiced oil so the spices bloom in the fat. For char, sear in batches over high heat without stirring constantly; for hands-off cooking, roast on a preheated sheet at 425°F about 15 min, then add beans and finish. Rest the chicken, then slice against the grain.

name: Peruvian-Style Grilled Chicken with Green Sauce
summary: Grill cumin-lime marinated chicken; serve with a creamy yogurt-cilantro green sauce.
technique_notes: Rub with a vinegar-cumin-paprika-garlic paste and marinate at least an hour. Cook slow over indirect/cooler heat skin-side up to render fat, then finish skin-down over direct heat to crisp and char. The green sauce is blended raw (cilantro, lime, jalapeño, yogurt) - make it fresh and keep it cold.

name: Shrimp and Avocado Salad
summary: Toss poached shrimp with avocado, tomato, and a lime-cilantro dressing over greens.
technique_notes: Poach the shrimp gently just until they curl into a C and turn pink (a tight O means overcooked), then shock in ice water. Add the avocado and dress only at the last moment to prevent browning and mush.

name: Turkey and Black Bean Chili
summary: Simmer lean turkey with beans, peppers, and tomato in a smoky chili spice blend.
technique_notes: Saute onion, carrot, and pepper 6-8 min, then bloom garlic, chili powder, and cumin in the oil 1 min before liquid for depth. Lean turkey has no fat to render, so start with oil and brown about 5 min. Deglaze the browned bits, then simmer covered 30 min and uncovered 30 min to thicken.

name: Chana Masala (Chickpea Curry)
summary: Simmer chickpeas in a tomato-onion masala with ginger and warm spices; serve over brown rice.
technique_notes: Build a deeply browned onion-spice-ginger-garlic-tomato masala before the chickpeas go in - that base is the flavor. Add chickpeas with a little water and simmer uncovered 15-20 min until thick and stew-like. Stir in garam masala and lemon off the heat to finish.

name: Tandoori-Style Chicken with Cucumber Raita
summary: Roast yogurt-and-spice marinated chicken; serve with cooling cucumber raita and brown rice.
technique_notes: Use a two-stage marinade (lemon and salt first, then yogurt and spices) and slash the thighs so it penetrates; marinate at least 2 hours. Broil in the upper third, flipping every 4 minutes until 165°F; most charring happens in the first 10 minutes. Grate, seed and drain the cucumber for the raita.

name: Red Lentil Dal with Spinach
summary: Simmer red lentils with turmeric, ginger, and tomato; wilt in spinach and finish with a spice tempering.
technique_notes: Start lentils in room-temperature water with no salt (prevents graininess); skim foam and simmer uncovered 20-30 min until creamy. Don't skip the tarka: bloom whole spices in hot ghee/oil and pour over at the end, reserving some to spoon on top. Stir spinach in last, 3-5 min.

name: Turkey Meatballs with Marinara over Whole Wheat Pasta
summary: Bake herbed turkey meatballs, simmer in marinara, and serve over whole wheat pasta.
technique_notes: Don't overmix or pack the meatballs; grated onion, egg and bread crumbs keep lean turkey moist. Brown on all sides, about 5 minutes, then pour off excess oil and finish simmering gently in the marinara 15-20 minutes so they stay tender and the flavors blend.

name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Sausage with Peppers and White Beans
summary: Roast chicken sausage with peppers and onions, toss with white beans and a splash of vinegar.
technique_notes: Brown the sliced sausage hard (only 1-2 min per side, then remove) and sauté aromatics in the residual fat. Drain the white beans but don't rinse them - the starchy liquid makes the sauce. Simmer beans 4-5 min, then wilt greens and return the sausage at the very end so the beans stay intact.

name: Cobb-Style Salad with Grilled Chicken
summary: Arrange grilled chicken, egg, avocado, and tomato over greens with a light vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Prep each component separately and arrange in rows, serving the vinaigrette on the side to dress at the table. Herb-rub the chicken and grill 5-6 min per side to 160°F, then rest 10 minutes before slicing. Keep avocado tossed in lemon to hold its color. Everything goes on cold.

name: Spinach and Feta Frittata
summary: Bake eggs with wilted spinach, scallions, and feta into a sliceable frittata.
technique_notes: Wilt the spinach and wring out all liquid (cheesecloth/towel) or the frittata weeps. Heat oil until shimmering so eggs don't stick, set the bottom on the stovetop about 4 min, then bake at 375°F about 8 min until the top no longer jiggles. Rest a few minutes before slicing.

name: Moroccan Salmon with Chermoula
summary: Coat salmon in a cilantro-cumin chermoula and roast; serve with couscous or farro and greens.
technique_notes: Chermoula is a raw blended herb sauce - toast the cumin and coriander seeds first, then blitz with herbs, lemon and garlic, adding water to a drizzling consistency (can be made ahead). Roast salmon skin-side down at 400°F (200C) for 15-20 min just to medium. Drizzle some over and serve the rest on the side.

name: Spanish Chickpea and Spinach Stew (Garbanzos con Espinacas)
summary: Simmer chickpeas and spinach with smoked paprika, cumin, and tomato until thick and silky.
technique_notes: Cook onion, garlic and smoked paprika in oil until softened and slightly browned before adding tomato. Wilt the spinach in a handful at a time, then simmer the chickpeas with their canned liquid (it gives body) about 30 min until thick. Finish off the heat with EVOO and a few drops of sherry vinegar.

name: Turkish White Bean Stew (Fasulye)
summary: Stew white beans with carrot, onion, and tomato paste; brighten with lemon and parsley.
technique_notes: Cook the tomato paste until it darkens and loses its raw edge before adding liquid, then simmer gently so the beans stay intact. Brighten with lemon and parsley off the heat.

name: Chicken Fattoush Salad
summary: Toss crisp greens, cucumber, tomato, and grilled chicken with a sumac-lemon dressing and toasted pita.
technique_notes: Bake split pita brushed with oil and sumac at 350F about 15 min until crisp, then break into pieces. Whisk a lemon-sumac vinaigrette, toss in the pita with the vegetables, and let stand 15 min so it soaks up dressing. Grill seasoned chicken 3-4 min per side; slice thin over the salad.

name: Baked Trout with Lemon and Herbs
summary: Roast trout with lemon, garlic, and fresh herbs; serve with a grain and greens.
technique_notes: Pat fillets dry and bake skin-side down at 400F for 10-12 min, checking at 10. Pull at about 140F internal (carryover brings it to a safe 145F) just as the flesh turns opaque and flakes. Tuck lemon and herbs over the fillets; keeping skin on holds it together. Finish with more lemon.

name: Garlic Shrimp with Zucchini and Quinoa
summary: Saute shrimp in garlic and lemon with ribboned zucchini; serve over quinoa.
technique_notes: Don't overcook the shrimp (a C shape, not a tight O). Cook the zucchini hot and fast so it doesn't go soggy and watery, and add the garlic late so it doesn't burn. Finish with lemon off the heat.

name: Greek Baked Fish (Psari Plaki)
summary: Bake white fish over a bed of stewed tomatoes, onions, and herbs in olive oil.
technique_notes: Soften sliced onions ~7 min, add garlic and canned whole tomatoes, break them up and simmer 10-15 min until thickened. Season the fish and squeeze lemon over it, then nestle into the sauce and spoon sauce on top. Bake at 400F just until it flakes (15-25 min). Finish with parsley and more lemon.

name: Caprese Farro Salad
summary: Toss cooked farro with tomatoes, a little fresh mozzarella, and basil in a balsamic dressing.
technique_notes: Boil farro in salted water about 20 min, then strain and rinse with cold water so it cools before mixing. Tear the basil by hand and chop the mozzarella; combine with quartered cherry tomatoes and finish with good olive oil, salt, and pepper. Serve right away or refrigerate.

name: Minestrone Soup
summary: Simmer a vegetable, bean, and small-pasta soup in a light tomato base with herbs.
technique_notes: Saute the onion-carrot-celery soffritto ~8 min, add garlic, then tomatoes, beans, and broth and simmer covered 20 min. Stir in pasta and cook uncovered ~10 min. If making ahead, cook the pasta separately and add per bowl, since it absorbs the broth as it sits. A parmesan rind adds depth.

name: Ratatouille with White Beans
summary: Stew eggplant, zucchini, peppers, and tomato; fold in white beans for a protein-rich main.
technique_notes: Cook each vegetable in stages so each browns instead of stewing: onion+pepper 5-7 min, then eggplant 4-6 min until browned in places, then zucchini 3-5 min, removing each. Return everything with the white beans and tomatoes, cover, and cook 8-10 min just until tender.

name: Salmon Patties with Lemon Yogurt over Greens
summary: Pan-sear herbed salmon patties; serve over dressed greens with a lemon-yogurt sauce.
technique_notes: Flake cooled cooked salmon, bind with egg and crushed crackers, and mix gently until just combined so it stays tender. Form patties, coat, and refrigerate about 1 hour so they hold together. Pan-fry in oil and butter over medium, undisturbed, about 7-8 min per side until golden and crisp.

name: Chicken Shawarma Bowl
summary: Roast shawarma-spiced chicken; build bowls with brown rice, chopped salad, and tahini sauce.
technique_notes: Toss the thighs with the shawarma spices, lemon, and olive oil; refrigerate a couple hours or overnight if you have time. Sear in a cast-iron skillet over medium, spread out, ~5-6 min, then toss and cook another 5-6 min, going longer for browned, crusted edges. Rest before slicing thin.

name: Harissa Chicken with Couscous
summary: Roast harissa-glazed chicken and peppers; serve over whole wheat couscous with herbs.
technique_notes: Couscous is steamed: pour 2 cups boiling stock per 1 cup couscous, cover off the heat, rest 5 min, then fluff and stir in herbs. Sear the spiced chicken hard for char on both sides, then baste with harissa and move to indirect heat to finish to 165F so the glaze doesn't burn. Rest 10 min, slice on the bias.

name: Za'atar Roasted Chicken Thighs with Vegetables
summary: Sheet-pan roast za'atar chicken with tomatoes and onion; finish with lemon.
technique_notes: Roast at 425F: massage za'atar-garlic-lemon oil into the meat and under the skin, nestle thighs among the vegetables, cover with foil ~25 min, then uncover ~30 min until skin browns and crisps. Rest 5-10 min; finish with parsley and a pinch more za'atar.

name: Greek Yogurt Chicken Salad Wrap
summary: Bind shredded chicken with yogurt, celery, and herbs; roll into a whole wheat wrap with greens.
technique_notes: Use cooled diced chicken and pat add-ins dry so the wrap doesn't get soggy. Toast the almonds, whisk the yogurt dressing separately, then toss to coat; chilling 2 hours (or overnight) deepens the flavor. Layer greens against the wrap as a moisture barrier, or assemble just before eating.

name: Hummus and Roasted Veggie Power Bowl
summary: Top quinoa with hummus, roasted vegetables, and chickpeas; drizzle with lemon-tahini.
technique_notes: Roast the vegetables until caramelized; cool components if packing for lunch. Rinse quinoa to wash off bitter saponins, simmer 1 cup quinoa in 1.75 cups water ~15 min, then rest covered 10 min and fluff. Store parts separately and assemble cold. Thin tahini with lemon and water to drizzle.

name: Lightened Chicken Tikka Masala
summary: Simmer yogurt-marinated chicken in a tomato-spice sauce lightened with yogurt; serve over brown rice.
technique_notes: Marinate chicken in spiced salted yogurt, but don't over-marinate (4-5 hrs max; the yogurt/lemon acids start cooking the meat). Broil or grill flesh-up ~8 min until charred but still raw inside, rest 10 min, then finish in the simmering sauce ~10 min. Char the aromatics for smoky depth.

name: Palak Chana (Spinach and Chickpea Curry)
summary: Simmer chickpeas in a pureed spinach-ginger-spice sauce; serve over brown rice.
technique_notes: Dry-toast cumin seeds ~1 min until popping. Build a browned aromatic base, then add ground spices and cook ~2 min before the tomatoes and chickpeas; simmer ~10 min. Stir spinach in only at the very end and just wilt it off the heat to keep it green. Flavor deepens if made ahead.

name: Vegetable Bibimbap
summary: Top brown rice with sauteed and seasoned vegetables and a fried egg; serve with a light gochujang sauce.
technique_notes: Season each vegetable separately rather than together. Sauté carrots in sesame oil 1-2 min; wilt spinach ~30 sec, then squeeze out excess water so the bowl isn't watery. Crisp the rice in a hot pan, arrange veg in sections around a runny-yolk egg, then break the yolk and mix to bind.

name: Thai Red Curry with Tofu and Vegetables
summary: Simmer tofu and vegetables in a red curry with light coconut milk; serve over brown rice.
technique_notes: Press the tofu first. Sauté onion and pepper, then cook the curry paste with ginger ~2 min until fragrant before adding coconut milk; simmer ~10 min until vegetables are tender-crisp. Don't skip the sugar - it balances the paste. Add lime, tofu and basil off the heat.

name: Chicken Adobo
summary: Braise chicken in soy, vinegar, garlic, and bay until tender; serve over brown rice with greens.
technique_notes: Sear the chicken first, then toast garlic, bay and peppercorns in the rendered fat 30-60 sec before adding the liquids and scraping up the fond. Once the vinegar is in, let it simmer before stirring. Simmer uncovered ~20 min to 165F, then broil ~3 min per side for crisp skin.

name: Chili-Lime Shrimp Tacos with Slaw
summary: Sear chili-lime shrimp; tuck into tortillas with a crunchy cabbage-lime slaw and avocado.
technique_notes: Sear the seasoned shrimp hot and fast, just until firm and opaque (~3-5 min), then pull off the heat so they don't overcook. Toast the tortillas in a dry skillet until the edges brown - it deepens flavor and keeps them from tearing. Dress the slaw only just before serving so it stays crunchy.

name: Cuban Black Beans and Brown Rice
summary: Simmer black beans with sofrito and cumin; serve over brown rice with a squeeze of lime.
technique_notes: Build a sofrito: sauté onion and green pepper ~5 min until wilted, then garlic ~1 min until fragrant. Simmer the beans slowly and uncovered until very tender for a creamy texture, adding the sofrito and vinegar partway through. Mash a few beans to thicken; brighten with vinegar at the end.

name: Southwest Quinoa Salad
summary: Toss quinoa with black beans, corn, peppers, and avocado in a cumin-lime dressing.
technique_notes: Rinse quinoa, then simmer covered 15-20 min until liquid is fully absorbed; spread to cool so it isn't mushy. Whisk the lime-vinegar-cumin-oil dressing in the bowl first, fold in beans, corn and peppers, then stir in the cooled quinoa. Add avocado last.

name: Greek Turkey Burgers with Tzatziki
summary: Grill turkey burgers studded with feta and spinach; top with cucumber-yogurt tzatziki.
technique_notes: Squeeze spinach dry and don't overmix; feta keeps lean turkey (93%) moist. Form four patties, oil the grill rack and grill over medium-high about 4-6 min per side to 165F. A thumbprint dimple keeps them from doming; don't press while cooking.

name: Mediterranean Sheet-Pan Chicken and Vegetables
summary: Roast chicken with seasonal vegetables, olive oil, oregano, and lemon on one pan.
technique_notes: Cut veg by density and spread in a single uncrowded layer so each piece touches the hot pan and chars instead of steaming. Toss with lemon-oregano-garlic dressing; roast thighs at 425°F about 35 min to 165°F, then broil a couple minutes for color. For chicken breast, cube and roast at 400°F ~20 min.

name: Balela (Mediterranean Chickpea and Bean Salad)
summary: Toss chickpeas and beans with tomato, parsley, and mint in a lemon-olive oil dressing.
technique_notes: Dry the herbs and beans well, then toss with a zesty olive oil, lemon juice, white wine vinegar, garlic and sumac dressing. Leave it aside at least 30 minutes so flavors meld before serving. Best at room temperature, though it can be covered and chilled until ready.

name: Sicilian Cauliflower Pasta
summary: Roast cauliflower and toss with pasta, a little raisin and pine nut, garlic, and chili.
technique_notes: Deeply brown the cauliflower for nutty flavor (traditional versions simmer it tender, then break it into a sauce). Plump raisins, bloom saffron and soften toasted pine nuts in the starchy cooking water, finish pasta just shy of al dente in the pan, and top with toasted breadcrumbs for crunch.

name: Misir Wot (Ethiopian Red Lentil Stew)
summary: Simmer red lentils with onion and berbere into a richly spiced stew; serve with greens and brown rice.
technique_notes: Cook finely diced onions in spiced butter (niter kibbeh) over medium-high 8-10 min until golden - note: real recipes use fat here, not dry. Add garlic, tomato and berbere, cook 5-7 min, then simmer red lentils covered ~40 min until soft. Stir in more niter kibbeh and berbere at the end.

name: Harira (Moroccan Lentil and Chickpea Soup)
summary: Simmer lentils and chickpeas in a spiced tomato base finished with lemon and cilantro.
technique_notes: Soften onion, celery and carrot in olive oil, then bloom the spices 1-2 min. Add crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, lentils, chickpeas and cilantro; simmer ~45 min until legumes are very tender, adjusting liquid so it stays pourable. Thicken near the end with broken vermicelli or rice; finish with lemon.

name: Gigantes Plaki (Greek Baked Giant Beans)
summary: Bake large white beans in a tomato-herb sauce until creamy; serve with greens and feta.
technique_notes: Pre-cook (or use canned) giant/butter beans, then build a chunky tomato sauce by softening onion, carrot, celery and garlic before adding tomatoes and herbs. Simmer the beans in it briefly, then bake uncovered at 375°F for 20-30 min until thickened and the top turns golden.

name: Grilled Chicken Skewers with Chimichurri
summary: Grill chicken skewers and vegetables; spoon over a bright herb chimichurri.
technique_notes: Keep the acid (red wine vinegar) in the chimichurri, not the marinade - acidic marinades turn grilled chicken chalky. Pulse parsley/herbs, garlic, vinegar and oil coarsely (source uses a processor, not fully smooth). Cut chicken into 2-inch chunks, grill on separate skewers ~10 min turning once, then spoon sauce over.

name: Seared Tuna Niçoise-Style Plate
summary: Sear tuna rare; plate with blanched green beans, potatoes, egg, and a dijon vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Tuna is best rare: pat dry, season, and sear about 2 min per side, rest 5 min, then slice 1/2-inch thick against the grain. Cook the other components separately - steam potatoes ~15 min, green beans ~5 min to tender-crisp - and compose the plate with a lemon-shallot-Dijon dressing.

name: Pan-Seared Halibut with Romesco
summary: Sear halibut and serve over a roasted red pepper, tomato, and almond romesco sauce.
technique_notes: Halibut is lean and dries out fast: pat it bone-dry, sear in a hot pan undisturbed until it releases on its own, and pull it at just-opaque since it carries over off the heat. Romesco is blended from roasted peppers and tomato with toasted almonds and a little bread for body - make it ahead, it improves as it sits.

name: South Indian Fish Curry (Meen Kuzhambu)
summary: Simmer white fish in a tangy tomato-tamarind and light-coconut curry with South Indian spices.
technique_notes: Bloom garlic in oil ~30s, then curry leaves ~30s on medium-low; add ground spices in quick succession ~1 min, splashing in water if you smell scorching. Slip fillets into the spiced oil to coat, then add tamarind water; once it boils, simmer uncovered only ~1 minute - poach gently, don't over-reduce or boil hard, which toughens fish.

name: Thai Steamed Fish with Lime, Garlic, and Chili
summary: Steam white fish over aromatics and finish with a punchy raw garlic-lime-chili dressing.
technique_notes: Steam just until the fish flakes (about 8-10 min depending on thickness) - steaming is unforgiving of overcooking, so check early. Make the lime-garlic-chili-fish-sauce dressing raw and spoon it over after steaming so it stays bright and sharp; don't cook it.

name: Shrimp Saganaki (Greek Shrimp with Tomato and Feta)
summary: Bake shrimp in a garlicky tomato sauce topped with feta until just pink and bubbling.
technique_notes: Reduce the tomato sauce until thick before the shrimp go in, then add the shrimp and cook only until they turn pink and curl into a C - they keep cooking in the hot sauce, so pull early. Marinate the shrimp in oil, oregano, dill, and garlic first; simmer the sauce 15 min; sprinkle feta on at the end off-heat.

name: Cajun Blackened Tilapia with Corn and Black Beans
summary: Coat tilapia in Cajun spice and sear hard for a blackened crust; serve with a corn and black bean salad.
technique_notes: Blackening needs a screaming-hot cast-iron pan and a dry, well-spiced fillet: press the paprika-cayenne-thyme rub on and let it sit (up to 30 min). Heat oil until almost smoking; don't move the fillet until the crust sets (about 3 min per side). Tilapia is thin and cooks fast, so flip only once. Use good ventilation.

name: Spanish Mussels in Smoked-Paprika Tomato Broth
summary: Steam mussels open in a smoky tomato, garlic, and white-wine broth.
technique_notes: Scrub the mussels and discard any that stay open when tapped before cooking, and any that stay shut after. Build the tomato-paprika broth first, then add the mussels, cover, and steam just until they open (4-6 min) - pull them as they open so they don't turn rubbery. Bloom the smoked paprika briefly off high heat so it doesn't scorch.

name: Sicilian Swordfish with Tomato, Caper, and Mint
summary: Grill or sear swordfish and top with a quick Sicilian tomato, caper, olive, and mint relish.
technique_notes: Swordfish dries out if overcooked, so use thick steaks (1-1.5 in). Dredge in flour for color, then use unilateral cooking: brown hard on the first side ~5 min, flip only ~2 min to 130-135F. Build the tomato-caper-olive sauce in the same pan, then nestle the fish back to warm through. Keep the relish bright, not over-reduced.

name: Roasted Cauliflower With Feta, Almonds and Olives
summary: Roast cauliflower until deeply browned; toss with feta, toasted almonds, and olives.
technique_notes: Roast at 425°F for 25-30 minutes, tossing once halfway for even browning. Toast the almonds separately in a dry skillet over medium-low, stirring often so they don't burn, 4-5 min. Toss the roasted cauliflower with feta and olives while warm; finish with lemon and flaky salt. Just as good at room temperature, so it holds for make-ahead.

name: Kale and Butternut Squash Bowl With Jammy Eggs
summary: Roast butternut squash, sauté kale, and serve over grains with jammy soft-boiled eggs and a tahini drizzle.
technique_notes: It's steamed, not roasted: boil the eggs in 1 inch of water, covered, exactly 6 min, then cool. Pour off to ¼ inch, lay in ½-inch squash slices (5 min), then pile broccoli, then kale on top; cover and steam until squash is tender and broccoli crisp-tender, 2-4 min. The yogurt-lemon-ginger-sesame sauce tastes sharp alone but balances on the vegetables.

name: Cherry Tomato and White Bean Salad
summary: Marinate cherry tomatoes and white beans in olive oil, red wine vinegar, and basil; serve at room temperature.
technique_notes: Halve the cherry tomatoes and toss raw with rinsed cannellini, chopped basil, and good EVOO - no cooking. Use a robust extra-virgin olive oil; its flavor carries the dish. Drizzle aged balsamic and flaky salt at the very end, just before serving. Serve at room temperature; keeps about 2 days though basil may discolor.

name: Lemony Asparagus Salad With Shaved Cheese and Nuts
summary: Shave raw or blanched asparagus thin, toss with lemon vinaigrette, and top with shaved hard cheese and toasted nuts.
technique_notes: Toast the nuts at 350°F for 5 min, then chop. Steam whole trimmed spears just tender, ~5 min, and drain (don't shave into raw ribbons). Macerate minced shallot in the lemon juice with salt 2 min before whisking in the oil, then stir in nuts, cheese and herbs. Dress just before serving.

name: Mediterranean Fish Chowder With Potatoes and Kale
summary: Simmer white fish and potatoes in a light tomato-fennel broth with kale.
technique_notes: Soften onion, celery and carrot ~5 min, then melt in minced anchovies and garlic 1-2 min before the tomatoes and paste (cook 10-15 min). Simmer potatoes 30 min in the broth with a bouquet garni (bay, thyme, orange zest) and saffron. Cook the kale separately; add it and the fish at the end and simmer just 5 min.

name: Mackerel With Lemon Olive Oil and Tomatoes
summary: Roast or pan-sear mackerel and serve over garlicky burst tomatoes with lemon and herbs.
technique_notes: It's roasted, not seared: make lemon oil by warming EVOO with lemon zest just to the first bubble, off heat, 20+ min. Roast fillets at 425°F on a bed of basil, drizzled with the oil and topped with olives, tomatoes scattered around, 5-7 min (thin) up to 12 (thick). Finish with more lemon oil and basil.

name: Citrusy Roast Chicken With Pears and Figs
summary: Roast chicken thighs over sweet pears and figs with lemon and fresh thyme until caramelized.
technique_notes: Rub a garlic-orange-zest-rosemary paste over and under the skin, then chill uncovered 4 hrs to overnight. Roast the whole chicken at 450°F for 30 min, then add halved fresh pears and figs cut-side down to the hot pan and roast 15-25 min more. Rest the chicken 10 min. Finish with a raw orange-garlic-sherry-vinegar relish and parsley.

name: Cucumber-Tomato Salad With Seared Halloumi and Olive Oil Croutons
summary: Sear sliced halloumi golden, toss with cucumber-tomato salad, and top with crunchy olive oil croutons.
technique_notes: Croutons are baked, not fried: toss torn bread in EVOO, bake at 400°F 18-22 min. Salt the cucumbers and weight with ice to firm and drain; salt tomatoes separately and pour off liquid. Steep smashed garlic in the EVOO, then discard before dressing. Sear halloumi in a little oil over medium-high ~1 min per side; add croutons and halloumi last.

name: Greens and Beans With Toasted Crumbs
summary: Sauté hearty greens and white beans in garlicky olive oil; top with crispy pan-toasted breadcrumbs.
technique_notes: Keep it brothy: don't mash the beans. Gently simmer scallions, chard stems, celery, garlic and thyme in the olive oil 12-15 min to infuse without browning. Add green beans, lima beans, chard leaves, a pinch of sugar and water; simmer ~8 min until just tender. Toast crumbs dry ~4 min and scatter on last so they stay crisp.

name: Farro With Blistered Tomatoes, Pesto and Spinach
summary: Blister cherry tomatoes in olive oil, toss with cooked farro, pesto, and fresh spinach.
technique_notes: Boil rinsed farro uncovered in well-salted water ~30 min until tender, not mushy. Roast cherry tomatoes and red-onion wedges with oil at 400°F, 25-30 min, until blistered. Toss the hot farro with olive oil, pesto and lemon, then stir in raw spinach to wilt. Fold in the tomatoes and juices; add mozzarella. Great warm or cold.

name: Slow-Roasted Citrus Salmon With Herb Salad
summary: Slow-roast a whole salmon fillet in olive oil with citrus slices; top with a bright herb salad.
technique_notes: Roast skinless salmon low and slow at 300°F on a bed of sliced lemon and orange, drizzled generously with olive oil, 25-35 min, just until opaque at the edges and barely flaking — the fat bath makes it hard to overcook. Toss the herb salad (parsley, dill, tarragon) with lemon juice and flaky salt right before serving.

name: Saffron Salmon Kababs
summary: Marinate salmon in saffron, lemon, and onion, then grill or broil on skewers.
technique_notes: Grind the saffron with a pinch of sugar, then steep in 2 Tbsp just-boiled water 5 min to draw out color. Marinate 1-inch salmon cubes only 30 min (lime starts to cure the fish) in saffron, lime, garlic and spices. Grill medium-high on flat skewers, turning every couple minutes and brushing with marinade, ~10 min total.

name: Roasted Halibut With Lemons, Olives and Rosemary
summary: Roast halibut over a bed of lemon slices, olives, and rosemary until just cooked through.
technique_notes: Roast at 450°F just until opaque, about 10 min — halibut is lean and overcooks fast, so pull it early. Top each fillet with a rosemary branch and thin lemon slices, scatter kalamata olives around, and go easy on salt. If the lemons haven't singed, broil 1-2 min. Drizzle with more olive oil.

name: Salmon and Couscous Salad With Cucumber-Feta Dressing
summary: Roast salmon and serve over couscous with a creamy blended cucumber-feta dressing and herbs.
technique_notes: Uses pearl couscous: toast it dry 3-4 min, then simmer in plenty of salted water 8-10 min and drain — not a 1:1 pour-over. Roast salmon at 400°F ~18 min, then flake. The dressing is stirred, not blended: thick yogurt thinned with water, lime, diced Persian cucumber, feta and herbs. Toss warm couscous with arugula to wilt it.

name: Simmered Beet Greens With Roasted Beets, Lemon and Yogurt
summary: Roast beets and simmer their greens separately; serve together over garlicky yogurt with lemon.
technique_notes: Roast scrubbed beets at 425°F in a covered dish with ¼-inch water until knife-tender (30-60 min by size), then slip off the skins while warm. Wilt the greens in a hot skillet in just the clinging water, add oil, cover and simmer 5 min. Add lemon only just before serving or they dull. Stir mashed garlic into drained yogurt.

name: Puttanesca Chickpea-Tomato Salad
summary: Toss chickpeas and tomatoes with olives, capers, and anchovies in a bold puttanesca vinaigrette.
technique_notes: No cooking — just stir tomatoes, chickpeas, kalamata olives, capers, grated garlic, lemon and coarsely chopped Parmesan with olive oil. The briny capers and olives stand in for the usual anchovies (omit Parmesan to make it vegan). Let it sit 10 min up to 2 hours so the beans drink up the juices; adjust salt and lemon. Keeps 2 days.

name: Italian Wedding Soup
summary: Simmer chicken meatballs with orzo and vegetables in a light broth; finish with baby spinach and parmesan.
technique_notes: Build the soup base by cooking onion, carrot, celery, and garlic in olive oil until translucent (4-5 min) before adding broth. Cook the orzo directly in the broth (not separately) and pull it when just tender — about 9 min — before the meatballs go in. Add meatballs and baby spinach together at the very end and cook only 2-4 min; spinach needs no chopping and wilts almost instantly. Make meatballs larger than marble-size (easier to form and more satisfying). Batch-make and freeze meatballs ahead so the soup comes together in 20 min. Finish with a generous drizzle of olive oil and parmesan at the table.

name: High-Protein Caprese Chickpea Salad
summary: Toss chickpeas, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, and mozzarella in a Dijon-balsamic vinaigrette with fresh basil.
technique_notes: The dressing is the key: whisk balsamic vinegar, olive oil, Dijon mustard, and grated (not minced) raw garlic — the Dijon emulsifies and the grated garlic melts in without chunks. For added texture, toast half the chickpeas in a dry pan until crispy and toss them in at the end so they stay crunchy. Use pearl mozzarella whole; it holds its shape and size better than torn fresh mozzarella. The salad holds well for up to 3 days refrigerated, making it ideal for meal prep — add basil just before serving.

name: Chickpea & Quinoa Bowl with Roasted Red Pepper Sauce
summary: Build grain bowls with quinoa and chickpeas topped with a blended roasted red pepper, almond, and spice sauce.
technique_notes: The sauce is the dish: blend jarred roasted red peppers with slivered almonds, olive oil, garlic, paprika, and cumin until fairly smooth — it's similar to romesco but lighter (no bread, more cumin). If it feels too thick, add a splash of water. Make the sauce and the seasoned quinoa base separately ahead of time, then assemble just before serving so the components stay distinct. Toss the cooked, cooled quinoa with kalamata olives, red onion, and olive oil to season it before plating.

name: One-Skillet Garlicky Salmon and Broccoli
summary: Sear salmon pieces with garlic, set aside, then cook broccoli and peppers in the same pan; finish with lemon juice and tamari.
technique_notes: Use a nonstick skillet so the salmon releases cleanly. Cook salmon pieces in a single layer with half the sliced garlic over medium-high heat 4-5 min, stirring occasionally, then transfer to a plate — don't wipe the pan so the salmon flavor stays. Add broccoli, bell peppers, the remaining garlic, and a tablespoon of water; cover and cook 4-5 min until just tender-crisp. Cut broccoli into bite-sized pieces so it cooks through in time. Stir in lemon juice and tamari off the heat, then fold salmon back in gently so it doesn't break apart. Request center-cut salmon at the fish counter for uniform thickness. Salmon is done at 130-135°F (it carries over to 145°F off heat).

name: White Bean Salad With Roasted Cauliflower
summary: Roast cauliflower until caramelized, toss with white beans, herbs, and a bright lemon dressing.
technique_notes: Roast sliced cauliflower at 400°F on the top rack until well browned, 20-25 min; the caramelization carries the dish. Whisk a sharp dressing of shallot, Dijon, lemon, red wine vinegar and ground fennel. Toss with the white beans and celery, careful not to crush them, and rest 30 min to meld. Add parsley and scallions; serve at room temperature.

name: Chicken Kebabs with Turmeric and Chile
summary: Marinate chicken thigh chunks in turmeric, chile, lemon and saffron, then grill slowly on skewers.
technique_notes: Marinate thigh chunks with sliced onion, red chile powder, turmeric, garlic powder, a pinch of saffron, lemon juice and olive oil 3 hours to overnight. Discard the onion, thread onto skewers, and grill slowly over low, even heat with the grate ~6 inches from the coals, basting with marinade and turning until browned all over, 15-20 min.

name: Baked Chicken with Hibiscus BBQ Sauce
summary: Dry-rub chicken legs and roast, then glaze with a homemade sweet-tart hibiscus barbecue sauce. Occasional treat only — the sugary sauce is off-profile for weight-loss and uric-acid goals, not a weekly staple.
technique_notes: Rub legs with seasoned salt, garlic and onion powder, paprika and thyme; roast at 425F about 30 min until golden but shy of done. Brush generously with the sauce, return 5 min to 165F. For the sauce, simmer hibiscus, vinegar, spices, brown sugar and ketchup 20-25 min until it streams off a spoon, then strain, pressing hard on the solids.

name: Classic Gazpacho (Chilled Tomato Soup)
summary: No-cook blended chilled soup of ripe tomatoes, cucumber, pepper and olive oil for hot days.
technique_notes: Layer torn bread in a bowl, then salted tomatoes, cucumber, onion, pepper, garlic and herbs, more salted tomatoes, then oil and sherry vinegar; rest 30 min so salt draws out juices that soak the bread. Blend on high a full 3 minutes for silk, then push through a fine-mesh strainer with a ladle. Chill; serve cold.

name: Cold Cucumber Yogurt Soup
summary: Blender-only chilled soup of cucumber and Greek yogurt with herbs, lemon and a little garlic.
technique_notes: Blend cucumbers, Greek yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, basil, dill, one raw garlic clove, salt and a touch of honey until smooth; the honey offsets the lemon tang and raw-garlic bite. Chill at least 4 hours (or overnight) so it thickens and flavors meld. Go easy on garlic since it stays raw; garnish with reserved cucumber and herbs.

name: Mahi-Mahi Skillet with Tomato-Lemon Sauce
summary: Pan-seared mahi-mahi finished in a quick blistered-tomato, garlic and lemon pan sauce.
technique_notes: Pat fillets very dry and salt well so they sear instead of steam. Sear in olive oil and a little butter over medium-high 3-4 min untouched per side until golden, then set aside. Blister cherry tomatoes ~4 min, add shallots and garlic 1 min, then stock, vinegar and lemon; simmer 4 min. Return fish to ~137F internal; finish with zest and basil.

name: Acqua Pazza (Tomato-Garlic Poached Halibut)
summary: Firm white fish gently poached in a garlicky tomato-and-olive broth with olive oil.
technique_notes: Soften shallots in olive oil, add garlic 1 min, deglaze with white wine 2-3 min, then water, salt and chili. Add tomatoes and a basil sprig; simmer 15 min until soft and reduced by half. Slip in seasoned halibut and olives, simmer gently ~5 min, then turn off heat and let residual heat finish it until flaky. Use firm fish (halibut, cod, snapper), not delicate or oily.

name: Wild Rice and Lentil Salad
summary: Hearty grain-and-legume salad with arugula, caramelized shallots, toasted almonds and pomegranate.
technique_notes: Simmer wild-rice blend and brown lentils together in broth until tender and absorbed, ~45 min, then rest. Meanwhile caramelize thinly sliced shallots low and slow in olive oil 30-45 min, and toast almond slivers dry 2-3 min. Toss warm grains with arugula, mint and almonds; dress with olive oil and balsamic and top with pomegranate. Good warm or cold for packed lunches.

name: Greek Yogurt with Honey and Walnuts
summary: Thick strained yogurt drizzled with honey and topped with toasted walnuts — a uric-acid-friendly breakfast or light dessert.
technique_notes: Use thick full- or low-fat strained Greek yogurt (low-fat dairy actively lowers uric acid). Toast walnuts dry in a skillet a few minutes until fragrant to deepen flavor, then drizzle a modest amount of honey just before serving so it stays glossy. Keep honey light to stay on-profile; add cinnamon or a few cherries for sweetness without extra sugar.

name: Melitzanosalata (Greek Eggplant Dip)
summary: Char whole eggplant over open flame until fully blackened, drain well, then mix with garlic, parsley, lemon, and EVOO for a smoky rustic dip.
technique_notes: Char eggplant on gas burner or under broiler 10-20 min, turning with tongs until skin is fully blackened and flesh is very soft. Cool in a bowl. Peel, chop, drain in a colander 10 min to remove excess liquid. Mix by hand with garlic, onion, parsley, and lemon. Chill 30 min before serving.

name: Muhammara (Roasted Red Pepper & Walnut Dip)
summary: Roast peppers at 425°F, steam-peel in covered bowl, then blend with walnuts, pomegranate molasses, Aleppo pepper, tomato paste, and sumac into a thick savory-sweet dip.
technique_notes: Roast peppers at 425°F for 30 min, turning once. Cover in bowl with plastic wrap 5 min to trap steam; peel when cool. Blend roasted pepper strips with walnuts, tomato paste, breadcrumbs, pomegranate molasses, Aleppo pepper, and sumac until smooth paste. Serve at room temperature drizzled with EVOO.

name: Fattoush Salad
summary: Fry pita in olive oil until browned; season with sumac. Toss with chopped vegetables, parsley, mint, and a lemon-sumac-allspice vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Fry torn pita in 3 tbsp olive oil in skillet over medium heat, tossing frequently until golden. Drain on paper towels; season with salt and sumac while hot. Dressing: whisk lemon juice, EVOO, sumac, pinch cinnamon, and allspice. Add crispy pita just before serving to preserve crunch.

name: Gigantes Plaki (Greek Baked Beans)
summary: Sauté onion, carrot, celery in EVOO; add tomatoes, herbs, cinnamon, and bay leaf; stir in canned beans and bake at 375°F until thickened and lightly golden on top.
technique_notes: Sauté onion, carrot, celery, garlic in EVOO 5-7 min until softened. Add diced tomatoes with juices, parsley, thyme, oregano, red pepper flakes, cinnamon, and bay leaf. Add drained beans and cook 5 min on high. Transfer to oven at 375°F and bake 20-30 min until thickened and top browns. Finish with EVOO and crumbled feta.

name: Tzatziki (Greek Cucumber Yogurt Dip)
summary: Grate cucumber, squeeze completely dry in cheesecloth, then fold into strained Greek yogurt with garlic, white vinegar, and EVOO; chill before serving.
technique_notes: Grate cucumber finely (food processor or box grater), toss with salt, then squeeze in cheesecloth until very dry — there will be a lot of liquid. Combine minced garlic, white vinegar, and EVOO in bowl first, then fold in drained cucumber and yogurt. Refrigerate at least 30 min — improves texture and lets flavors meld.

name: Horiatiki (Traditional Greek Salad)
summary: Combine chunked tomatoes, cucumber, green pepper, olives, and red onion; dress with EVOO and red wine vinegar; top with slab feta and crumbled oregano.
technique_notes: Soak red onion slices in ice water with a splash of red wine vinegar for 10 min to mellow raw bite. No whisked dressing — pour EVOO and vinegar directly over vegetables. Top with large slabs of block feta (not crumbled) for authentic texture. Finish with dried Greek oregano.

name: Shirazi Salad (Persian Cucumber & Tomato)
summary: Small-dice cucumber, tomatoes, and onion; drain tomatoes briefly in a colander; toss with dried mint, fresh herbs, sumac, lime juice, and EVOO.
technique_notes: Dice all vegetables very small (~1/4-inch) so they absorb the dressing quickly. Drain diced tomatoes in a colander briefly before combining to avoid a watery salad. Key spice is dried mint — use it alongside fresh parsley and dill. Dress with lime juice, EVOO, and sumac. Chill 30 min for bolder flavor.

name: Sautéed Broccoli Rabe with Garlic and EVOO
summary: Sauté sliced garlic in olive oil until golden; pack in broccoli rabe, add water, cover and steam until bright green; uncover to cook off liquid; finish with EVOO.
technique_notes: Trim bottom 1/2 inch of stems. Sauté sliced garlic in 1/4 cup olive oil on medium-low 2-3 min until lightly golden. Pack in broccoli rabe; add 1/4 cup water, cover, and steam on medium-high 3-4 min until bright green. Remove lid, season with salt and red pepper flakes, cook 2-3 more min to evaporate water. Finish with EVOO drizzle.

name: Harissa Lentil & White Bean Salad
summary: Simmer lentils uncovered until tender; build a tomato-harissa sauce with onion, garlic, and warm spices; fold in lentils and white beans; cool and top with raw onion, carrot, mint, and EVOO.
technique_notes: Simmer lentils in 3:1 water uncovered ~20 min; do not add salt until after draining or lentils harden. Sauté majority of onion with garlic; add tomatoes, coriander, allspice, sugar, and 2 tbsp vinegar; cook 5 min. Stir in harissa and lentils/beans; cook 5 more min. Stir in 1 tbsp vinegar off heat. Cool before serving.

name: Roasted Eggplant Caprese with Basil Vinaigrette
summary: Salt eggplant slices 30 min to draw out bitterness; roast with tomatoes at 425°F; layer with mozzarella and basil; warm briefly to melt cheese; drizzle with blended basil vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Salt eggplant slices generously and rest 30 min — they sweat out bitterness and soften. Pat completely dry before roasting. Roast at 425°F for 10-15 min. Layer tightly in baking dish (eggplant, tomato, mozzarella, basil); return to oven 7-10 min just until cheese melts. Blend basil vinaigrette separately and spoon over.

name: Italian Garlic Green Beans
summary: Steam green beans briefly until bright green; sauté in garlic-infused olive oil until well coated; season and finish with a drizzle of EVOO.
technique_notes: Steam trimmed green beans in 1/2 cup water covered 2-3 min until bright green. Drain and wipe pan dry. Sauté sliced garlic in olive oil on medium-low 1-2 min until lightly golden — do not burn. Add beans, toss to coat thoroughly in garlic oil, cook 2-3 more min. Season with salt and optional red pepper flakes; finish with EVOO.

name: Marinated Roasted Red Peppers
summary: Char bell peppers under broiler until fully blackened; steam-peel; slice and marinate in garlicky EVOO with vinegar and herbs.
technique_notes: Broil or char whole peppers on gas burner, turning frequently, until skin is blackened all over. Place in covered bowl 10-15 min to steam (makes peeling much easier). Peel under cold running water; remove seeds. Slice and marinate in EVOO, garlic, and red wine vinegar at least 30 min. Serve at room temperature with pita or as part of a mezze spread.

name: Quick Pickled Vegetables (Mezze Turshi)
summary: Pack thinly sliced vegetables in jars with a hot vinegar-salt brine; refrigerate; ready to eat in 1-2 hours and best after overnight.
technique_notes: Slice vegetables thinly and uniformly for consistent pickling. Brine: 1 part white vinegar to 1 part water, 1 tsp salt per cup of liquid, optional pinch of sugar. Pour brine over packed vegetables while still hot. Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate. Add a raw beet slice for natural pink color on turnips. Usable after 1 hr, best after 24 hrs.

name: Whipped Feta with Honey and Herbs
summary: Blend block feta and cream cheese in food processor with EVOO, honey, and lemon zest until very smooth; serve topped with EVOO, herbs, and warm pita.
technique_notes: Use block feta packed in brine — not pre-crumbled — for creamiest texture. Pulse feta and cream cheese first before adding EVOO, honey, and lemon zest; blend until very smooth. Whipped feta firms in the refrigerator — bring to room temperature before serving. Top with EVOO, za'atar, walnuts, or pomegranate seeds.

name: Za'atar Roasted Cauliflower with Tahini
summary: Toss cauliflower florets with za'atar and EVOO; roast at high heat until edges are charred; drizzle with lemony tahini sauce and parsley.
technique_notes: Cut cauliflower into evenly sized florets — crowding the pan causes steaming instead of charring. Single layer on sheet pan; roast at 425-450°F for 25-30 min, flipping once halfway, until edges are deeply golden with char. Thin tahini with lemon juice, garlic, and water until pourable consistency. Drizzle over warm cauliflower just before serving.

name: Chickpea & Spinach Stew (Espinacas con Garbanzos)
summary: Fry garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika in EVOO; add tomatoes and chickpeas; simmer 10 min; fold in spinach until just wilted; finish with sherry vinegar.
technique_notes: Fry sliced garlic in generous EVOO until golden, then add cumin and smoked paprika and toast 30 seconds before adding tomatoes. Simmer tomatoes 5 min to concentrate. Add drained chickpeas and cook 5-10 min. Add spinach in two batches, folding in until just wilted. Finish with sherry vinegar or lemon juice off heat.

name: Baba Ganoush (Smoky Eggplant & Tahini Dip)
summary: Char whole eggplants until completely blackened and collapsed; drain bitter liquid 15-20 min; mix flesh with tahini, garlic, and lemon into a smoky creamy dip.
technique_notes: Char eggplants directly over gas flame or under broiler, turning every 5 min until completely collapsed and skin is fully blackened. Drain in colander 15-20 min to remove bitter liquid. Scoop flesh and mix with tahini, garlic, and lemon — do not over-blend; some texture is preferred. Garnish with EVOO, smoked paprika, and parsley.

name: Fasolakia Lathera (Greek Braised Green Beans in Olive Oil)
summary: Classic lathera main: green beans and potato stewed velvety in olive oil and tomato, served with feta and bread.
technique_notes: Saute onion in a full 1/3 cup olive oil per pound of beans (don't skimp or it turns watery), coat potatoes then beans in the oil, add tomato and parsley. Add hot water only to half-cover; simmer covered ~40 min until no water remains. Rest covered 10 min. Fresh or frozen beans, never canned.

name: Spanakorizo (Greek Spinach and Rice)
summary: Creamy one-pot spinach-rice staple finished with lemon, olive oil, and feta — half a pound of greens per serving.
technique_notes: Wilt spinach first with lemon juice, drain. Saute onion, add spinach, dried mint, dill, 2/3 cup warm water; boil, add rice, simmer covered ~20 min. Medium-grain rice (not long-grain or basmati) for creaminess; cook spinach WITH the rice so flavors meld.

name: Greek Eggplant-Feta Rolls in Tomato Sauce
summary: Roasted (not fried) eggplant slices rolled around feta, baked in a smooth tomato sauce — vegetarian comfort main.
technique_notes: Puree onion-garlic for a smooth sauce; simmer with crushed tomatoes 20 min, stir in mint/parsley off heat. Slice eggplant lengthwise 1/4 inch, salt 20 min, pat dry, brush with oil, roast 15-20 min at 350F until pliable. Roll around feta batons, sauce over, bake 25-30 min. Rest 20 min.

name: Greek Chickpeas and Rice with Lemon and Tahini
summary: One-pot monastery-style legume main: creamy rice and chickpeas simmered in a lemon-tahini broth. Fast, pantry-friendly, vegan.
technique_notes: Whisk 1 tbsp tahini with juice of 1.5 lemons and 3-4 tbsp water before starting. Saute onion then garlic; stir rice and chickpeas to coat in oil. Add tahini-lemon mix, bay leaf, ~1.5 cups chickpea liquid or water; simmer 15-20 min until absorbed. Medium-grain rice gives creaminess.

name: Greek Black-Eyed Peas and Spinach Stew
summary: Thick beans-and-greens tomato stew — quick-cooking black-eyed peas need no soak, finished with lemon and feta.
technique_notes: Boil dry black-eyed peas with a bay leaf 30-35 min until almost done; drain. Saute onion, carrot, pepper 5 min, wilt in spinach, then add beans, crushed tomatoes, only 3/4 cup hot water; simmer 25 min until thick. Stir in 2 tsp breadcrumbs at the end to thicken. Lemon squeeze to serve.

name: Revithosoutzoukakia (Greek Chickpea Patties in Tomato Sauce)
summary: Falafel's softer Greek cousin: chickpea-tomato patties pan-fried then simmered in an intense tomato-paste sauce.
technique_notes: Pulse chickpeas with fresh tomato — keep it grainy, do not over-mix. Knead in flour 1-2 tbsp at a time until soft but shapeable; flour-coat patties. Shallow-fry in 1/4-inch olive oil ~2 min per side. Simmer tomato paste sauce 10 min, then finish patties IN the sauce 1-2 min so they soften.

name: Strapatsada (Greek Scrambled Eggs with Tomato and Feta)
summary: 14-minute egg main that's really tomatoes-with-eggs — a full vegetable serving per egg; classic Greek light supper.
technique_notes: Saute onion until soft, garlic 1 min, then chopped tomato 5 min until soft. Pour in beaten eggs, RAISE the heat, stir quickly ~2 min without smashing the tomatoes (chunky, not a puree). Stir in feta off the heat; salt last since feta is salty. Finish with oregano and mint.

name: Kolokithokeftedes (Greek Zucchini Fritters with Feta and Herbs)
summary: Herb-loaded zucchini-feta fritters, shallow pan-fried in olive oil — classic mezze that pairs with tzatziki or yogurt.
technique_notes: Grate zucchini, salt in colander 10 min, then squeeze hard by hand — removing water is the make-or-break step. Mix with feta, herbs, eggs, breadcrumbs; flour+baking powder gradually to a thickish batter. Shallow-fry in 1/3 inch olive oil, ~2 min then 1-2 min per side. Eat fresh; they soften as they cool.

name: Greek Braised Broccoli with Garlic and Tomato
summary: Five-ingredient lathera-style braise: broccoli goes silky in olive oil and browned tomato paste; works as side or light main.
technique_notes: Saute garlic 1 min in 1/4 cup olive oil, then brown the tomato paste in the oil for deep flavor. Briefly saute carrots then broccoli to seal, add only 1/4 cup water, cover, simmer low ~30 min until soft and water is absorbed — never cover the broccoli with water. Rest covered 15 min; generous lemon.

name: Ribollita (Tuscan White Bean, Kale, and Bread Soup)
key_ingredients: ciabatta or crusty whole grain bread
summary: Hearty Tuscan soup where pureed and whole white beans, kale, and olive-oil-toasted bread meld into a thick, satisfying one-pot meatless dinner; leftovers reboil beautifully for lunch.
technique_notes: Toast torn bread with EVOO at 400F ~10 min. Soften onion-celery-carrot, garlic 30 sec. Puree 1 cup beans with 1/2 cup of the brothy tomato mix to thicken. Simmer with parmesan rind, thyme, bay 20 min; add beans and kale, then half the bread to soften. If making ahead, hold bread until reboiling.

name: Ezo Gelin Çorbası (Spicy Turkish Red Lentil and Bulgur Stew)
summary: Thick Turkish lentil-bulgur stew finished with a sizzling mint and Aleppo pepper oil — about 17g fiber per bowl, deeply savory with no meat.
technique_notes: Simmer rinsed red lentils in hot water ~25 min, skimming foam. Stir in bulgur, tomato paste, pepper paste, dried mint; cook 10-15 min more until bulgur is tender, thinning with water as needed. Finish with lemon juice plus an infused oil: warm EVOO with dried mint and Aleppo pepper 30-40 sec, pour over.

name: Garlic Chickpea Spinach Soup with Lemon and Pecorino
summary: Brothy 40-minute chickpea soup where partially mashed chickpeas and their canning liquid create body without cream; spinach and lemon added at the end keep it bright.
technique_notes: Reserve 1/2 cup chickpea canning liquid. Saute onion and garlic 5 min; bloom cumin, coriander, paprika 30 sec. Roughly mash chickpeas in the pot to break some. Add broth plus reserved liquid, boil 5 min, simmer 30 min partly covered. Stir spinach and parsley in off heat 1 min; finish lemon, EVOO, pecorino.

name: Pisto (Spanish Ratatouille-Style Vegetable Stew)
summary: Manchegan stewed vegetables built by staggered sauteing so nothing turns mushy; serve as a half-plate vegetable side, or top with a fried egg for a vegetable-forward main.
technique_notes: Stagger additions in hot EVOO: onion 5 min, peppers 4 min, garlic 30 sec, eggplant 3 min, zucchini ~3 min until browning starts. Add tomatoes, paprika, cumin; reduce ~10 min at medium until tender. Off heat, stir in sherry vinegar and parsley — the vinegar finish is essential lift.

name: Bamya (Egyptian Okra and Tomato Stew)
summary: One-skillet okra simmered in allspice-scented tomato sauce until silky; a classic Egyptian vegetable side over rice, hearty enough to anchor a vegetable-forward plate.
technique_notes: Saute onion, garlic, and chile 4-5 min. Saute okra 5-7 min over medium-high BEFORE liquid hits — this pre-sear tames sliminess. Add crushed tomatoes and 1/2 cup water, lay tomato slices on top, boil, then simmer mostly covered on low 20-25 min until soft. Finish with lime juice.

name: Foul Mudammas (Egyptian Fava Beans with Garlic and Lemon)
summary: Ten-minute mashed fava beans dressed with a pounded garlic-chile-lemon sauce and EVOO; protein- and fiber-rich vegetarian lunch that is good warm or at room temperature.
technique_notes: Warm canned favas with 1/2 cup water, season with salt and cumin, then partially mash with a fork — keep texture. Pound garlic and hot pepper to a paste (mortar or knife), stir in juice of a whole lemon, pour over beans. Generous EVOO drizzle; top with parsley, diced tomato. Serve with pita and sliced vegetables.

name: Eggplant Rollatini with Ricotta and Pesto
summary: Baked (not fried) eggplant slices rolled around a pesto-ricotta filling in marinara — a lighter vegetarian take on lasagna flavors at under 200 calories per serving.
technique_notes: Slice eggplant lengthwise 1/4-inch; salt on paper towels 20 min, rinse, dry. Pre-bake oiled slices at 375F ~8 min just until pliable — do not overcook or they tear. Fill each with ~2 tbsp ricotta-pesto mix, roll from short end, seat in sauced dish, top with marinara; bake ~30 min. Rest 10 min before serving.

name: Farro Salad with Arugula, Walnuts, and Feta
summary: Chewy whole-grain salad tossed while the farro is still warm so it drinks up the dressing; packs well and keeps 2-3 days, ideal make-ahead office lunch.
technique_notes: Simmer 1 cup farro in 3 cups salted water 20-40 min depending on type; drain well and pat dry so the salad is not watery. Toss farro still somewhat warm with arugula, tomatoes, peppers, walnuts, and three herbs — warmth slightly wilts greens and absorbs vinaigrette. Feta last. Dressing keeps up to 2 weeks jarred.

name: Egyptian Skillet Onion Chicken
summary: Three-ingredient braise where a mountain of deeply caramelized onions becomes the sauce for skinless chicken thighs; needs only rice or pita alongside.
technique_notes: Caramelize 4 sliced onions in EVOO 10-15 min until collapsed and deep golden — manage heat so they never burn. Push onions to the edges, sear salted skinless thighs meaty-side down uncovered until browned both sides. Add just 1/4 cup broth or water, cover, medium-low 25-30 min to 165F.

name: Greek Lemon Rice with Orzo and Dill
summary: Pilaf-style lemon rice where toasted orzo adds nutty depth; the bright, herby quarter-plate starch for Greek chicken, fish, or lathera vegetables.
technique_notes: Rinse rice until water runs clear, soak 10 min, drain. Toast orzo with onion and garlic in EVOO until colored, then coat rice. Add lemon juice and 2 cups broth, boil, then low covered 15-20 min. Rest covered 5-10 min off heat — do not disturb. Fold in parsley, dill, lemon zest at the end.

name: Sautéed Spinach with Lemon
summary: Ten-minute wilted spinach side — the fastest way to put a half-plate of leafy greens next to any protein.
technique_notes: Heat EVOO over medium, sauté sliced garlic just 30 seconds until fragrant. Add spinach in batches, letting each wilt before adding more, 2-3 min total. Off heat, drizzle lemon juice and season — adding lemon off heat keeps it bright and prevents dull army-green spinach. Serve warm or room temperature with lemon wedges.

name: Lemon Broccoli with Pecorino
summary: Sheet-pan roasted broccoli with browned edges, finished with lemon and salty pecorino — 6g fiber per serving.
technique_notes: Roast at 400F: cut florets, peel stems and slice into 1/4-inch coins so nothing is wasted. Toss with EVOO, salt, pepper on a sheet pan; roast 25-30 min until edges brown and stems pierce easily. Toss with lemon juice while hot, then shower with grated pecorino and serve warm.

name: Batata Harra (Lebanese Spicy Potatoes)
summary: Crispy spiced potato cubes tossed with garlic, paprika-tomato coating, and fresh cilantro — a mezze-table standard.
technique_notes: Crisp 1/2-inch potato cubes in 350F olive oil 3-5 min until golden (or roast for a lighter version); drain well. Separately cook minced garlic in 2 tbsp olive oil until just golden, then toss in potatoes with paprika, tomato paste, and chili powder to coat. Off heat, stir in chopped cilantro and salt.

name: Greek Fava (Yellow Split Pea Purée)
summary: Ikarian legume purée served as a mezze or side — 15g fiber and 14g protein per serving from a handful of pantry ingredients.
technique_notes: Simmer rinsed yellow split peas with chopped onion, water covering by a few inches, 30-45 min until thick and mushy; drain any excess. Beat in crushed garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil while warm until thick and blended. Cool, season, garnish with paprika and an EVOO drizzle.

name: Barley Salad with Feta and Roasted Vegetables
summary: Warm grain salad where the feta roasts alongside the vegetables until caramelized; barley's beta-glucan makes it a cholesterol-lowering lunch that packs well.
technique_notes: Roast cherry tomatoes, bell pepper, zucchini, and cubed feta together at 425F with EVOO 30-40 min until juices release and caramelize — roasting the feta alongside is the trick. Meanwhile boil pearled barley about 30 min until tender. Combine warm with lemon juice, fold in basil ribbons. Good warm or chilled.

name: Ensalada de Garbanzos (Spanish Chickpea Salad)
summary: No-cook chickpea salad with a cumin-scented lemon vinaigrette and briny capers — 10g fiber, holds up well made ahead for office lunches.
technique_notes: No-cook: toss rinsed canned chickpeas with diced cucumber, red bell pepper, halved cherry tomatoes, red onion, parsley, mint, and capers. Whisk dressing of EVOO, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, and ground cumin — the cumin makes it Spanish. Chill 15 min to meld, adjust seasoning, garnish with crumbled feta.

name: Greek Chop Chop Salad
summary: Chunky-cut Greek salad with romaine and a creamy feta-yogurt dressing — one bowl, no cooking, five minutes of knife work.
technique_notes: Everything cut chunky: thick-sliced quartered cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, rough-chopped red onion and romaine, halved kalamatas, 1/2-inch feta cubes. Toss gently with fresh mint leaves, a pinch of dried oregano, and creamy feta dressing (blended feta, yogurt, lemon, EVOO). Assemble just before serving so the romaine stays crisp.

name: Turkish Bulgur Salad Bowl (Kısır-Style)
summary: No-boil bulgur salad dressed with sautéed tomato-paste onions, pomegranate molasses, and lemon — 9g fiber and sturdy enough to pack.
technique_notes: Pour 2/3 cup hot water over 1 cup fine bulgur, cover, rest 15 min to absorb — no boiling. Sauté onion translucent, add tomato paste 3 min, then cumin and pepper flakes off heat. Fold into bulgur with pomegranate molasses and lemon juice, then chopped lettuce, scallion, parsley, tomato.

name: Baked Chickpeas with Zucchini and Fresh Herbs (Ikaria)
summary: Ikarian blue-zone bake layering chickpeas over vegetables and three fresh herbs — a massive 24g fiber and 25g protein per serving, no meat needed.
technique_notes: Layer quartered carrots and zucchini in a baking dish under mint, dill, parsley, diced onion, chopped tomato, and cooked or canned chickpeas. Add a cup of reserved chickpea broth, EVOO, and salt; bake at 350F about 15 min until golden, then stir and bake again until the top crisps.

name: Chickpea Stew with Spinach, Dill, and Turmeric
summary: One-pot turmeric-golden chickpea stew thickened with a little rice and finished with wilted greens and a cooling yogurt dollop — 12g fiber.
technique_notes: Cook onions in EVOO until golden, 7-8 min; bloom garlic, turmeric, pepper flakes 1 min. Add broth, water, and 1/4 cup rice; simmer 10-12 min. Add tomato sauce, diced tomatoes, chickpeas; simmer 10 more. Wilt in spinach, dill, cilantro 3-5 min. Serve topped with a dollop of Greek yogurt.

name: Creamy White Beans with Lemon, Garlic, and Parmesan
summary: Ten-minute skillet beans that turn creamy from parmesan and starch alone — the fastest legume main in the library; serve over greens or with crusty bread.
technique_notes: Ten-minute skillet: sizzle sliced garlic and pepper flakes in EVOO 1-2 min until lightly golden. Add canned cannellini and 1/4 cup broth; simmer gently 5-7 min until slightly reduced. Finish with lemon zest, juice, and grated parmesan stirred in until creamy. Garnish parsley; serve over greens or bread.

name: Italian Lentil Soup with Rosemary Oil and Roasted Leek
summary: Half-blended lentil soup — creamy but textured — crowned with a caramelized roasted leek half and rosemary oil; 17g fiber per bowl.
technique_notes: Soften onion, carrot, celery 5 min in EVOO; add garlic, then green lentils, broth, bay leaf. Simmer 30-40 min until tender. Remove half the lentils, blend the rest smooth, stir the whole ones back — creamy but textured. Top with roasted leek halves (400F, 15-20 min) and rosemary-infused oil.

name: Soufico (Ikarian Layered Vegetable Casserole)
summary: Ikaria's answer to ratatouille from Diane Kochilas: salted, pre-softened vegetables layered with grated tomato and baked until melting — a vegetable-forward centerpiece.
technique_notes: Salt eggplant, peppers, and zucchini in colanders 1 hour; wipe dry without rinsing. Lightly sauté (or oven-soften at 350F) each vegetable separately, plus onion-garlic. Layer in a Dutch oven with grated tomato, oregano, and salt between layers, pressing down each time. Drizzle EVOO on top; bake 350F 45-60 min until caramelized.

name: Greek Artichokes, Green Peas, and Potatoes (Anginares Lathera)
summary: Classic Cretan lathera: artichokes, peas, and potatoes braised in a lemony dill-olive oil broth that thickens into the sauce — two legume-vegetables in one pot.
technique_notes: Sauté artichoke hearts, green onions, and carrot rounds in EVOO 5 min. Add chopped dill, quartered potatoes, 1/2 cup lemon juice, and 2 cups water; simmer 20 min. Add peas for 10 more. Finish with a cornstarch slurry boiled 2 min to lightly thicken the lemony braising liquid into sauce.

name: Lentil Greek Salad with Dill Yogurt
summary: Cooked lentils layered with tomato, cucumber and a garlicky dill-yogurt sauce, assembled cold.
technique_notes: Build as separate meal-prep components and dress only at eating time — the salad waters out once tossed. Cook lentils barely tender (Instant Pot: 1 cup lentils to 3 cups water, 3 min high pressure, quick release, drain) so they hold shape cold. Dress with olive oil, lemon and a pinch of salt just before eating.

name: Baked Salmon over Lentils with Lemon Herb Sauce
summary: Lentils and quinoa oven-baked in broth, then salmon and vegetables roasted directly on top.
technique_notes: Bake rinsed lentils and quinoa in broth at 450°F for 45-50 minutes until almost cooked, then fluff. Lay salmon skin-side down on top with quick-cooking vegetables and return for ~10 minutes. Dense vegetables like sweet potato must be par-boiled first — 10 minutes will not cook them. Reserve half the lemon dressing to finish raw.

name: Cauliflower Rice Salad with Crispy Chickpeas
summary: Raw cauliflower pulsed into rice, tossed with roasted crispy chickpeas and a mustard-lemon dressing.
technique_notes: Roast oiled, spiced chickpeas at 400°F for 20-30 minutes until genuinely crisp and browned. Pulse cauliflower florets in a food processor about 20-30 pulses to a rice texture — work in batches or it turns to paste. Keep components separate until serving; once dressed it softens fast. Reserve some chickpeas to scatter on top.

name: Slow Cooker Lentil and Butternut Soup
summary: Lentils, split peas and squash slow-cooked, then partly blended with olive oil for a creamy body.
technique_notes: Cook everything except greens 5-6 hours on high or 7-8 on low. Blend ~4 cups of the soup with the olive oil and return it — the oil emulsifies into the starch and creates creaminess without dairy. Stir kale and parsley in off-heat. Finish with vinegar or lemon; flavor and texture improve on resting. Instant Pot: 6-7 cups broth, soup setting, 30 min.

name: Sheet Pan Spiced Chicken with Tzatziki and Peppers
summary: Cumin-paprika chicken and peppers roasted on one sheet pan, served family-style for building pitas or bowls.
technique_notes: Peppers need a head start: roast at 425°F for 20 minutes, stir and push to one side, then add marinated chicken to the empty side and roast 10 minutes more. Marinate the chicken at least 30 minutes (up to 24 hours). Squeeze grated cucumber dry before it goes into the tzatziki or the sauce turns watery.

name: Roasted Cauliflower over Whipped Hummus
summary: Spiced roasted cauliflower spooned over a thick swoop of homemade lemon-garlic hummus.
technique_notes: Roast spiced cauliflower at 425°F for 25-30 minutes. For genuinely smooth hummus, peel the skins off the chickpeas before blending (~20 minutes, but it is the whole difference) and blend far longer than feels necessary. Tahini is optional — oil, garlic, salt and plenty of lemon carry it. Serve hot or cold.

name: Pearl Couscous Skillet with Tomatoes and Chickpeas
summary: One-skillet braise of chickpeas and tomatoes with pearl couscous cooked directly in the sauce.
technique_notes: Soften shallot with cumin ~5 minutes, then mash some of the chickpeas against the pan — this is what makes the dish creamy rather than brothy. Add couscous with the liquid, cover and hold on low 6-8 minutes to al dente. It keeps absorbing liquid as it sits, so serve promptly or loosen with water when reheating.

name: Greek Baked Orzo with Kale and Feta
summary: Orzo simmered with kale and tomato in an oven-safe skillet, finished under feta in the oven.
technique_notes: Build in layers on the stove: onion 5 minutes, then garlic/pepper/kale/oregano 5 minutes until wilted, then tomato paste 1-2 minutes to caramelize before any liquid.
